description: Source-alignment record between the Claude skills in this repo and the Codex plugin port in email-love/codex-agents. Its job is to stop a fix from landing in one surface and silently never reaching the other. Update it whenever either surface ships a change that the other should mirror, and stamp lastAlignmentReview when you have checked the two are in sync.

codexPlugin.distributionModel: The public ChatGPT and Codex plugin is a reviewed snapshot. A GitHub push does not update directory users.
releaseChecklist: Port and validate the Codex plugin.
Tag and push the GitHub release.
Create or update a plugin version in the OpenAI submission portal and upload the final skills bundle.
Submit for review, then publish after approval.
Verify the public listing and test from a new chat or Codex task.
codexPlugin.note: GitHub is at v4.6.1 (2026-08-05, codex-agents commit 7e0b371a4fd847b2cd4f21b8f4707da2dfafc75f). v4.6.0 ported converter 1.43.1 and bundled the Email Love exporter MCP; v4.6.1 is the submission-preflight patch that adds the required mcpServers wrapper and HTTP transport in .mcp.json, corrects the skills-and-MCP submission wording, and keeps the portal suite at exactly five positive and three negative cases. The public directory remains v4.5.0 until v4.6.1 is uploaded through the With MCP submission path, reviewed, and published. Earlier alignment history remains recorded in the drift entries below.

drift.summary: Batch 13 (2026-08-10, postmortem from a Codex-run design system build; canvas fidelity mistaken for export fidelity). Converter 1.43.1 to 1.44.0: tri-state module status in batch reports (canvas/structure/exporter reported separately, deferred is a state never a pass); repair discipline block (measure before restructuring, never retry a render-disproven change, reconstruct after two patches, property-count comparison across repairs, resumable record); supplied source HTML authoritative for both breakpoints (DOM + media-query inventory before building, screenshots never override); Part A stacking decision three-way with RECOMPOSED option via observed visibility keys, explicit desktop-vs-mobile comparison for headers and footers, no invented mobile-alignment key; render-spec 4.2.2 inverse rule never CREATE a combined raster; stackColumns read-back-clean-but-render-wrong measured example.
drift.codexStatus: Not yet ported. HIGH RELEVANCE to Codex: the postmortem originated from a Codex-run build, so these fixes address failures observed on their surface directly. Batch with the next port spec.

Companion fixes shipped outside this repo: the mcp.emaillove.com authorize page copy now names the MCP connection and its capabilities (worker 0.46.1), and the help page gained a three-surfaces disambiguation section with connect commands (docs commit bd5ea9e).

drift.summary: Batch 12 (source parity, from the 180-module Ultimate EDS migration: five clean batch verifications while 26 modules disagreed with the source). Converter 1.42.0 to 1.43.0: new Group 0 parity-with-source gate run first on EVERY module (TEXT count + strings, image count + dimensions, alignment, band fills, against the audit's T/I census; three named resolutions only; batch reports OPEN with the parity table); serializer-and-builder pipelines fail totally and silently, so no sampling; type checks cover WEIGHT and each text style's NAME must match its read-back VALUE (five Regular-named styles built in Light put 271 nodes at 300 weight); the boundVariables empty-object trap generalised to name-the-value-that-fails-and-confirm-it-is-reachable (broken predicate reported zero violations on 242 black fills); text-on-background contrast check, never silently recolor a brand hex; new Group 6 asset identity (colourway vs band luminance, icon SET matching, sprite-sheet aspect detection, read placedOnNodeId back, never hand-transcribe bytes); per-module screenshots never optional; inventing content is a failure equal to dropping it. Audit 1.22.0 to 1.23.0: REQUIRED T/I content census column per inventory row; content margin measured from leaf content bounds never container padding (116 of ~180 sections were full bleed with padding 0, library set 40px too wide); margin distribution reported per category.

Batch 11. Converter 1.41.0 to 1.42.0: step 6's export sniff is agent-run by default via emaillove_export_figma on the Email Love MCP (mcp.emaillove.com), which compiles a bare mj-wrapper straight from the Figma file through the production /getHtml pipeline; operationType preview charges no export quota; output is golden-diffed against real plugin exports on every worker deploy (HTML-equivalent, dark CSS identical, on two live migration QA proofs). Phase 3's opening gate probes the MCP for the tool instead of asking who will click; the temporary-email-frame plus human-Export path is the fallback for out-of-coverage modules (mj-hero/social/navbar/table raise CoverageError) or an MCP without the tool; Deferred verification narrows to cases with neither tool nor human.

Batch 10 (live migration batches 2 and 3 reports). Audit 1.21.0 to 1.22.0: palette census samples text fills at segment level via getStyledTextSegments(['fills']) (mixed-run colours invisible at node level, measured #727272 miss); search other designs in the file for clean vector instances before writing a fused-asset rebuild remedy (measured: low-res capture had clean 4x vectors in another email); dark-mode mechanism corrected. Converter 1.40.0 to 1.41.0: dark CSS mechanism corrected from an export read: contentColor is painted on the WRAPPER and section/column fills are forced transparent, module fills ERASED not recolored, same flattening different mechanism, all rules stand (never-fill-a-group, neutral contentColor, per-node override); new hand-off statement that dark mode flattens module fills (cards do not read as cards, plugin limitation) and image backgrounds are not a workaround; inter-module gap single owner library-wide (wrapper paddingBottom from the spacing ladder, last module 0, zero double-duty section padding); mj-column has no background-image mapping, overlap art becomes in-flow mj-image with a BOOLEAN when source ships variants without it; mj-column-inner second genuine case (filled card + gutter, fill-less outer column carries the gutter padding).

Batch 9 (live migration: dark mode turned every card brand green; resolved in-file, rule extracted). Audit 1.20.0 to 1.21.0: contentColor is a global knob, never promote a single surface's brand hex into it; keep the neutral house default and record single-surface brand treatments (a band colored the same in both modes) as per-node override recommendations naming the module; promote to global only when the brand's dark treatment covers most content surfaces; show image-ink contrast against the recolored surface. Converter 1.39.0 to 1.40.0: theme-key priority sanity check mirroring the audit rule; sanctioned per-node override documented (write contentColor once on the module MAIN component, instances mirror shared plugin data, verified by instance read-back; conditional keys only, buttonContentColor/buttonTextColor stay the unconditional pair to avoid).

Batch 8 (updated Batch 1 report: export cycle completed, two new defects found only in exported HTML). Converter 1.38.0 to 1.39.0: never fill an mj-group (dark CSS has no group selector; fill-less children reset to background-color initial while text forced #FFFFFF = white-on-white; move fill to columns; filled group = step 5 FAIL); manage-preferences.com documented as second magic value with injection trap (plugin auto-links unlinked preference wording; backend swaps on Klaviyo only, literal third-party URL ships elsewhere; rule: always link preference text explicitly); third font-drift source in 3.3.1 (substituted family: source-measured column boundaries are stale, clone matches Arial not the replaced face; re-measure hug in the substituted face); band-with-decoration pattern (full-bleed mj-group, fill on copy column, art in decorative column with mobileStylesHideInMobileDevice; mj-section has no background-image mapping).

Batch 7 main body (two shakedown migrations on the plugin install; one ran the batch checks human-driven and caught two defects all arithmetic passed). Audit 1.19.0 to 1.20.0: cluster type tuples WITHIN a family never across (two families at one size = two rows); measure the button component never infer from palette census; apparent mj-* structure in source is a hint not a finding (narrow section = wrapper-padding constraint); get_metadata SSE limits (~80KB / non-ASCII) with use_figma chunked fallback. Converter 1.37.0 to 1.38.0: batch-check ownership established before module 1 + Deferred verification list when checks cannot run in-session; step 1 worker-vs-direct-tree-read decision (email-native sources read the tree); mask-from-geometry as first remedy for baked-in backgrounds (color keying fails at ~11 units/channel); 0.3.1 rewritten to two sanctioned exceptions (full-bleed bands + card/inset blocks) with band-edge invariant and group-sums-to-group note; 8.3 INSTANCE_SWAP snippet corrected for local components (node id + type COMPONENT); inline button construction (Figma rejects nested TEXT property remap); link-bearing text excepted from the 1.37.0 text-properties default (binding wipes hyperlink ranges); bordered groups pinned FIXED with width headroom (borders push column sum past 100 percent and wrap); group narrower-than-content-box + mobile viewport-spread notes; range writes read back via getStyledTextSegments; spacer fill clarified (bound SOLID when the spacer IS a band); Gelasio/Tinos metric clones + display-size caveat; step 5 read-back transport note.

Batch 7 (plugin shakedown migration, first finding): customer-facing copy gets TEXT properties BY DEFAULT. The old evidence gate ('a TEXT needs evidence the copy changes between sends') starved single-design sources to zero text properties, shipping a library read-only from the property panel and contradicting the Getting Started page (which says text is edited through component properties). New default: headlines/eyebrows/subheads/body/button labels get TEXT properties without evidence; boilerplate (legal, address, unsubscribe) stays unbound; evidence gate now applies only to BOOLEANs and INSTANCE_SWAPs. Range widens to 2-7; zero legitimate only for modules with no customer-facing copy. Step 5 Group 4 predicate enforces: every customer-facing text node reachable through a module-root TEXT property, violations by node id. Images unchanged (no image property type in Figma; fill-replacement is the documented workflow). Bumps converter 1.36.0 to 1.37.0.

Repo restructure per the packaging guide: three skills ship as ONE Claude Code plugin 'email-love' at plugins/email-love/ (skills at plugins/email-love/skills/{eds-converter,migration-audit,figma-builder}, frontmatter names shortened, descriptions untouched). Three DEPRECATED shim entries stay in marketplace.json under the legacy names pointing at the moved directories, so old installs and every shipped Staying-current check keep resolving; shim versions sync with each SKILL.md's version line every release. Per-skill plugin.json files removed (skill dirs stay plain). .skill release bundles keep legacy emaillove-* names. validate_repo.py reworked (bundle+shim validation, shim version sync, stale-URL detection), build.sh and .gitignore paths updated. Install is now: claude plugin install email-love@email-love. NOT a content change to either skill.
drift.codexStatus: No port needed: repo-layout change on the Claude side only. NOTE for future port specs: raw URLs now use plugins/email-love/skills/<short-name>/ paths; pin specs to a commit as always.

drift.summary: Verification consolidation (Andy-requested simplification): Phase 3 step 5 restructured from seventeen accreted prose checks into ONE read-back pass per module evaluating five predicate groups locally (shape and tags, sizing, geometry against foundations, fills and bindings, mobile data), violations by node id, plus one desktop screenshot. Step 6 renamed 'Batch checks': the mobile render (emaillove_preview_email) moves there beside the export sniff since both share the provisional-upload precondition and operate at batch level. New small-library allowance: 8 or fewer modules may run as ONE batch with one review before upload. No coverage lost; every measured case preserved compressed. Motivation: Figma round trips are the stated bottleneck and a 17-item list of separate walk instructions either costs N walks or gets skimmed. Bumps converter 1.35.0 to 1.36.0.

Batch 6 (change spec v2 from a live migration, 2026-08-03): mobile styles as first-class output with VERIFIED plugin-data schemas; dark mode stops mirroring light. (1) Converter gains 'Mobile Styles ARE shared plugin data' section: Schema A containers (mobileStylesPadding* + isPaddingActive, values inert without the flag), Schema B type (fontSize/lineHeight/letterSpacing + <prop>_mode='override' on the TEXT node, not the frame). REPLACES the batch 2 inline-key-table claim that mobile padding was node properties, which live observation disproved. New hard rule: never write a plugin-data key not observed from the plugin itself (an invented activation flag shipped 10px body copy). (2) Audit gains required 'Mobile styles' report section + two-anchor mobile ramp derivation (compression not scaling: single factor preserves desktop headline:body ratio which is the failure; anchors body->16-18, headline->26-30, floor 14, NO ratio test vs desktop). (3) Converter Phase 3 step 3 Part B rewritten: 'write the mobile styles', ALWAYS runs, replacing merge-the-twin-if-exists; includes 28px mobile bottom padding on non-last stacking columns. (4) Line heights PERCENT never PIXELS in all text styles (pixel freezes the mobile line box; measured 17px copy on 33px desktop line box) + setRangeFontName detachment trap with the one-segment verification. (5) Dark mode: six theme keys are DARK MODE values; old 'set equal to light colors' guidance verified WRONG against exporter dark CSS (ships light-on-light); house defaults #000000/#1F1F1F/#FFFFFF/#FFFFFF-button-#000000-label; audit Palette gains dark proposal with contrast ratios; render-spec 2.1 + inline table + send-readiness corrected. (6) Asset transparency: key UI icons for dark mode via border-connected flood fill, never brand logos (measured: keyed logo became illegible ink-on-ink); check surviving ink against #1F1F1F before keying. (7) Multi-column rows top-align by default (primary MIN + counter per content; independent exporter reads); batch 3 axis checklist updated to mark these intentional. structure.md mobile rows corrected. Bumps audit 1.18.1 to 1.19.0 and converter 1.34.0 to 1.35.0.

Batch 5 defect fix: multi-column gutter guardrail (task #52). Codex built a three-column component with zero column padding during a v4.1.0 shakedown; geometry validated (0-gutter columns sum to content-width trivially) but adjacent card headlines visually concatenated into one sentence. New Phase 3 step 5 blocking checklist bullet: a section with more than one column and zero horizontal column padding is a FAIL unless the source design has a measured zero gutter AND the batch report says so. Render-spec gets new subsection 3.4.0 'Multi-column gutters' generalising 3.4.1's spacing-on-one-side rule to every multi-column row. Failure signature named (headlines concatenate, card images touch, button a pixel from neighbour). Worked example for three equal cards. Do not infer card width by content/count unless source gutter is zero. 3.4.0 numbering keeps 3.4.1's Two Column Swap number stable. Bumps converter 1.33.2 to 1.34.0.

batch 4 defect fix (closes queue): Cloudflare 403 error code 1010 workaround (task #51). Phase 3 step 1 POST-to-worker instructions: if worker returns 403 with body 'error code: 1010', that is a Cloudflare browser check not an auth failure. Retry with a normal browser User-Agent header; Bearer/provider headers are correct. Rationale: Batch 4 hit this, every POST returned 403 with error code 1010, auth was irrelevant (empty Bearer, no Bearer, real token all failed identically); setting a browser User-Agent fixed it instantly. The 403 sat next to Bearer/license-key instructions so the natural conclusion was an auth problem. Closes batch 4 (10 defect fixes total). Bumps converter 1.33.1 to 1.33.2.

batch 4 defect fix: palette census clusters by ROLE + type ramp floor (task #50, enhancement to task #34). Palette census: sample text-node fills as well as background fills; same hex used as a band and as text on white are TWO theme tokens, not one, because the theme layer needs to move them independently. A palette built from fills alone finds bands and buttons and misses type. Type ramp: where the smallest cluster is below 12px, recommend a floor at 12 (or customer-confirmed floor). Rationale: Batch 4 shipped nav link #888888 and body color #222222 (used only on text) missing from the theme roles list, both added mid-batch; value-prop captions at ~11px standardised up to 12 mid-build. Bumps audit 1.17.0 to 1.18.0.

batch 4 defect fix: mj-navbar mapping documented (task #49). Render-spec section 6.1 note: when the worker returns mj-navbar, do not invent a mapping. Rebuild as one mj-text node whose characters carry every label, with setRangeHyperlink per label, separated by a normal space plus non-breaking spaces so gap survives HTML whitespace collapsing while line can break between labels but never inside one. Type styling from audit's Nav Link ramp entry. Two reasons this wins over alternatives past three items: reflows (a group of pinned columns cannot per 3.3.2), satisfies 'split single text run into N separately linked items' constraint without per-item column. Batch 4 met mj-navbar twice and improvised twice, ending at this shape both times; task #42's four-item nav shipped this way after group build failed twice. Bumps converter 1.33.0 to 1.33.1 (patch: documentation of a mapping previously punted on).

batch 4 defect fix: Figma cloud fonts have no Helvetica/Arial, build in Arimo (task #48). Phase 2 step 3 (Type mapping): call figma.listAvailableFontsAsync() and look for the target family by name before building. Figma environment for agents typically serves Google Fonts only (~1,900 families); Helvetica, Helvetica Neue, and Arial are all absent even though they are the most common email-safe answer. When target is Arial or Helvetica and unavailable, build in Arimo (metrically compatible Arial clone, identical advance widths). State consequence in foundations report: exporter writes fontName.family into font-family so export will say Arimo until family is swapped. Expect weight count to drop (Regular/Bold only from email-safe stack). Rationale: every agent-run migration whose customer picks the standard email-safe stack hits this; silent failure mode is building the ramp in Inter. Bumps converter 1.32.2 to 1.33.0.

batch 4 defect fix: open every exported PNG before uploading it (task #47). Render-spec 4.2.1 now has an explicit step between download and upload. Three failure modes: baked-in white (node with white background exports opaque, reads as white box on colored band; key white to transparency for line art, flood-fill surround for photographic cutouts), neighbour's content (check crop's far edge against adjacent column start, not source node declared width; a node can be wider than its visible content), and fused row not missing (already 4.2.2). Batch 4: 4 asset defects presented as layout bugs; the T-shirt baked in 28px of neighbouring column text, cost layout chased twice and component rebuilt once. Bumps converter 1.32.1 to 1.32.2 (patch: enhancement to existing 4.2.1 rule).

batch 4 defect fix: cap-height measurement method (task #46). New render-spec section 5.2.1: for settling type-size disagreements, crop tightly to one line, threshold to isolate glyphs, measure pixel ink height, compare against a known reference in same casing via size = knownSize * (measured/known). All-caps against all-caps, mixed-case against mixed-case (ascenders/descenders change ratio). Round onto ramp, never to nearest round number. Task #45's worker-vs-measurement rule now references this section. Inserted as 5.2.1 to avoid renumbering existing 5.3-5.6 references. Batch 4 references: 28px all-caps measured 20px ink; 36px mixed-case measured 33px. Bumps converter 1.32.0 to 1.32.1 (patch: method documentation).

batch 4 defect fix: STRUCTURE from worker, NUMBERS from measurement + ramp gaps at foundations (task #45). Phase 3 step 2 'unpinned drifts' bullet rewritten: worker is a good structure detector (columns, rows, stacking order, which things are buttons, sometimes structural fixes the source does not advertise) but not a measuring instrument (colors drift, sizes land on plausible round numbers rather than the ramp, unpinned fonts flatten to Arial). Take structure from worker, every color from source pixels, every size measured, every font pinned. A size the worker returns that is not on the audit's ramp is the loudest signal it guessed (per-module factor sneaking back in). Phase 2 step 3 Type specimen: a gap in the ramp is a decision for foundations, not batch 3; if the specimen shows a jump with nothing between it and the source has content that would sit in the gap, add the step now and record as a standardisation. Batch 4: 9 worker mismatches from #CCCCCC-for-#FFFFFF to four different wrong reds to a 40px headline where the ramp said 36. Foundations report predicted the ramp-gap cost verbatim and deferred anyway; three modules in batch 3 wanted the missing 20px step. Bumps converter 1.31.1 to 1.32.0.

batch 4 defect fix: unsubscribe.com magic link convention documented inline (task #44). Phase 2 inline plugin data key section now carries a 'Magic link values the exporter rewrites' table listing unsubscribe.com as the href the exporter substitutes with the selected ESP's unsubscribe merge tag at export time. Works on text, buttons and images. Never invent a placeholder URL, never hand-type an ESP merge tag unless customer asks. Send-readiness pass (task #35) updated to name unsubscribe.com as the default portable value. Rationale: Batch 4 invented `example.com/unsubscribe-placeholder`, escalated as legal problem not polish; customer pointed at help.emaillove.com/plugin/links/unsubscribe. Bumps converter 1.31.0 to 1.31.1 (patch: documentation of an existing plugin convention).

batch 4 defect fix: mobile visual via emaillove_preview_email, not get_screenshot (task #43). Phase 3 step 5 Visual bullet rewritten. Figma's canvas has no mobile breakpoint, so get_screenshot at 390px just renders desktop-shaped pixels at 390px; the old 'second screenshot pair at mobile width' instruction silently degraded to a recorded intention. Replaced with a headless render via emaillove_preview_email after the batch is uploaded provisionally to the plugin library. Fail conditions named: word broken mid-string (task #42 defect), image aspect ratio differs from desktop, stacked column carrying desktop gutter as indent, section that stacked where step 3 Part A recorded group (or vice versa). Order stated for migrations: build, upload provisionally, render, diff, only then open next batch. Rationale: three of the four batch 4 corrections were mobile-only, every one caught by the customer manually exporting screenshots. Bumps converter 1.30.0 to 1.31.0.

batch 4 defect fix (first of queue): mj-group columns shrink on mobile (task #42). New render-spec section 3.3.2 with resolved-width formula: `resolved = columnWidth / groupWidth * (mobileViewport - side padding)`. Per column: text carrier needs resolved >= widthOf(longest unbreakable word) * 1.05; fixed-aspect image needs resolved >= image natural width. Three remedies when a column fails (reflowing mj-text with setRangeHyperlink ranges, drop the group so columns stack, or hide with mobileStylesHideInMobileDevice). Phase 3 step 5 checklist gets a new group-columns-resolve-wide-enough bullet. Explicit: section 3.3.1 (font drift at pinned width) does not protect against this. Batch 4: four-item nav 137/86/133/89 in a 560 group rendered CHA/NGI/NG, G/E/A/R at 375px because the 86px GEAR column resolved to 51px. Invisible on canvas and desktop preview by construction. Bumps converter 1.29.0 to 1.30.0.

Batch 3 defect fix (closes queue): Getting Started page correctness + image workflow accuracy (task #40). Phase 2 Getting Started page section: the frame is vertical HUG with clipsContent OFF, never a fixed height (batch 2 shipped a 100px-fixed frame that clipped 940px of instruction text and the page rendered as the bottom edge of its own title). After writing the block, screenshot the whole page and confirm every line visible; a screenshot showing only the title is a fail. Image workflow described accurately: text edited through component properties (correct), images edited by selecting the image rectangle inside the instance and replacing its image fill (correct), never by detaching. Figma has no image component-property type so 'swap images using the component properties panel' is wrong and reads to a user as a workflow that does not exist. Phase 2 completion checklist Getting Started bullet updated with both requirements. Closes the Batch 3 queue (7 defect fixes total). Bumps converter 1.28.0 to 1.29.0. Closes Codex findings 1 and 5.

Batch 3 defect fix: button label MUST be exposed at module-root level (task #39). Phase 3 step 4 (properties): every module that contains a button re-exposes the foundation button's Label as a TEXT property on the module root, named `Button label` (single-CTA) or `Card N button label` (grid). Phase 3 step 5 checklist: any module with a button and no top-level Button label property is a fail; list by node id each button whose label is not surfaced at module level. Batch 2 shipped 18 buttons across 18 modules, each with a working label property on the foundation and none surfaced at the module the marketer instances, so a user following the Getting Started page could not change any CTA copy from the top-level property panel. Show button BOOLEAN is a separate decision from Label: add only where a sibling design in the source has that button absent, not speculatively. Bumps converter 1.27.0 to 1.28.0. Closes Codex finding 6.

Batch 3 defect fix: WCAG contrast table in Phase 2 foundations report (task #38). For every text-on-fill pairing the theme will render (textColor on backgroundColor, linkColor on backgroundColor, buttonTextColor on buttonContentColor, plus explicit text-on-brand pairings), compute WCAG contrast ratio and label pass/fail. Flag pairings that fail 4.5:1 for normal text or sit at 3:1 large-text floor. On a fail, name the darker semantic token that reaches threshold (batch 3's blue/700 #0078B4 = 4.83:1) or note designer needs to supply one. Rationale: Batch 2 shipped color/text/accent = #009EE2 at 3.00:1 on white and used it on 18px bold subheads (requires 4.5:1 AA). Bumps converter 1.26.0 to 1.27.0. Closes Codex finding 9.

Batch 3 defect fix: semantic-token bind count in Phase 3 step 5 (task #37). New verification line: every non-placeholder solid fill in a module resolves to a variable binding from the audit's Palette, not to a raw hex. Walk every fillable node, list unbound solid fills by node id with the raw hex and the role they should have (brand background, headline text, button background, divider, footer fill). Empty list is the only pass. Placeholder gray fills for editable image regions are the only allowed exception, each named as an intentional placeholder. Batch 2 shipped 43 unbound fills (31 real, 12 placeholder) and every downstream color change had to touch each of the 31 by hand, exactly the state a design system is meant to remove. Bumps converter 1.25.1 to 1.26.0. Closes Codex finding 8.

Batch 3 defect fix: enforcement teeth on Phase 3 step 5 structural rules (task #36). Rules that shipped violated on batch 2 (18 alignment axis mismatches, 18 untagged button TEXT children) get list-every-violation-by-node-id treatment; empty list is the only pass. The `name` key check explicitly includes the TEXT child of every mj-button (must carry mj-button-text). The alignment axis check names the exporter contract (mismatched axes render one way in Figma, another in HTML) and asks for each mismatch reported as `<node id>: primary=X, counter=Y`. Closes findings 2 and 7. Bumps converter 1.25.0 to 1.25.1 (patch: enforcement tightening on existing rules).

Batch 3 defect fix: send-readiness pass at hand-off (task #35). New '### Send-readiness pass on every campaign' step at the top of Hand-off in the converter. Before the hand-off conversation, walk every mainFrame campaign root and confirm safe to send. Per campaign root: all nine theme keys populated (not empty, since empty is not neutral and the exporter substitutes dark defaults), non-blank emailSubject and emailPreHeader, fallBackFontName is a single family name not a CSS stack, root has a non-generic name (QA roots renamed with 'QA only, do not send' prefix). Per mj-image: href is real URL or explicitly empty for decorative, altText is meaningful copy or empty for decorative. In footer: no placeholder legal, no 'Lorem ipsum', no literal 'Address' string, unsubscribe as merge tag or real URL not '#'. List every violation by node id under 'Send-readiness violations' heading. Empty list is the only pass. Rationale: Batch 2 or 3's Codex review found the delivered file had zero shared hrefs, zero shared altText, blank subject/preheader on all three campaigns, one root with blank lightThemeBackgroundColor, placeholder legal, and literal 'Address' string in footer. Closes Codex findings 3 and 4. Bumps converter 1.24.0 to 1.25.0.

Batch 3 defect fix (first of queue): palette census in audit (task #34). Audit Step 6 palette bullet rewritten from sampled ('their named paint styles') to a full census: enumerate every distinct fill hex in the file, cluster near-duplicates within a small delta (2-3 units per channel so #3C023C and #3C004A do NOT collapse but #009EE2 and #009FE1 do). Report Step 7 gets a new required 'Palette' section between Spacing system and Module inventory: source hex, count of fills using it, module list, plus proposed theme colors with every deviation from source hex listed with the delta so a designer approving the theme approves the drift too. Additional source colors not carried into theme roles listed at the bottom. Rationale: Batch 2 or 3's Codex review found four accent primitives lightened from source (Pink #C4014B -> #D03E75, Magenta, Teal, Orange) with no documentation of the drift, and two source colors absent from theme entirely (a decorative green, a bright blue). Palette section prevents undocumented drift and silent drops. Same shape as the spacing (task #27) and type ramp (task #30) censuses. Bumps audit 1.16.0 to 1.17.0.

Batch 2 defect fix (last of queue): inline plugin-data key table + precondition check (task #28). Adds a new '### Precondition check: confirm the references are present' at the top of Phase 2 that reads references/render-spec.md and references/structure.md before starting; on absent files, names what cannot be verified and directs the agent to fetch a fresh bundle or agree a reduced scope with the user (an earlier customer batch hit this four modules in and cost five rounds of design review). Then a new '### The shared plugin data keys the exporter reads (inline, load-bearing)' section carrying the complete `emaillove` shared plugin data key table inline (name, nodeType, nine theme keys on the mainFrame root, optional email meta, fullWidth, stackColumns, reverseStack, href, altText), with what goes where and what it does. Plus a 'Mobile behaviors that are NOT shared plugin data keys' section covering four mobile behaviors batch 2 spent rounds hunting for that turned out to be Figma-side: full-width mobile button (layoutSizingHorizontal='FILL' on mj-button), fluid-on-mobile image (width-relationship to column content width), mobile padding overrides (node properties), mobile column stacking (stackColumns or mj-group). Render spec keeps the prose, worked examples and rationale; the inline table is the irreducible contract that makes the skill functional even when a bundle ships without references. Closes the Batch 2 queue (5 defect fixes shipped, 1 was deprioritized after the packaging bug that caused the original symptom was fixed, this one lands anyway as belt-and-braces). Bumps converter 1.23.0 to 1.24.0.

Batch 2 defect fix: render-once-crop-locally + band-detection measurement techniques + nav bar worked example (task #32). Three additions across both skills. (1) Converter Phase 3 step 1: on an unstructured source, render the whole design at 1:1 once and crop locally per module rather than per-node get_screenshot (which returns loose rectangles without overlapping text, useless on layered z-order files). (2) Audit Step 5 pass 1: same band-detection technique used for finding module boundaries on unstructured pages (rows of pure canvas background between text/imagery are gaps between modules); record y-coordinates on source ref so Phase 3 crops the same pixels. (3) Converter Phase 3 step 5 visual check: on a module that comes out 20-40px too tall (Figma text renders taller than hand-placed boxes report), detect content bands in source PNG and rebuild PNG, diff them, derive exact padding corrections; deterministic two-pass loop instead of eyeballed nudging. (4) Nav bar worked example added to mj-group visual tells: a row of five or more nav links does NOT survive as a group (exporter divides body width by column count, per-link boxes narrower than a single word, breaks words mid-letter); ungrouped columns stack cleanly, one link per row. Batch 2: band detection got 24 of 28 modules onto source height; nav bar rule saves two attempts. Bumps audit 1.15.0 to 1.16.0 and converter 1.22.0 to 1.23.0.

Batch 2 defect fix: export sniff test added to Phase 3 (task #29). New Phase 3 step 6 'Export sniff test (once per batch)' between per-module verify (step 5) and batch report (now step 7). After individual modules pass step 5, pick one representative module (a multi-column one when possible, since mobile behavior lives in columns), drop a wrapper instance into a temporary email frame on Campaigns, click plugin's Export, read the HTML. Confirm four things: (1) body width matches foundations target email width, (2) `@media only screen and (max-width` block is present, (3) mobile classes exist for anything that should stack or go full-width (`mj-column-per-100`, `mj-b-full`), (4) per-section column widths plus gutters sum to intended content box (a `mj-group` that overflows shows up as a column-sum > body width). Record confirmations in batch report; on a fail, fix the defect Figma-side and re-export, do not open review. Rationale: every check in step 5 is Figma-side, and the plugin's exporter is what decides group overflow, button width, image scaling. Batch 2 spent five rounds reverse-engineering exporter behavior by pixel-measuring preview PNGs when one export read would have caught the group overflow, button width and fluid-image behavior together in the first batch. Step numbering shifts: old step 6 'Batch report and gate' is now step 7; the 'finishing a batch IS a stop' reference at the top of the skill updated. Bumps converter 1.21.0 to 1.22.0.

Batch 2 defect fix: render-node-not-fill constraint fires at asset export AND at module screenshot, plus logos-never-resized rule (task #31). Converter Phase 2 step 6 already carried the render-node-not-fill rule; Phase 3 step 1 (screenshot the module) now carries it too, because the mistake happens where the pipeline is. Batch 2 or 3's hero photograph was cropped out of a canvas render and the overlapping white card baked into the image, producing a ghost headline inside the picture that only surfaced at the visual check. Phase 3 step 1 now states: the module screenshot is for the worker to classify structure, not the source of image assets; any image asset a module carries is exported from its own node in isolation, not cropped from the module screenshot or a canvas render. A bulk canvas-crop pass for efficiency in either phase is the failure mode. Separately: Phase 2 step 6 adds 'logos have an intrinsic size and are never resized to fit', because a batch 2 'grow inset images to fill their column' pass stretched the footer logo to 191x68. Logo intrinsic size is the source of truth; do not stretch, scale up to match a hero, or fold into a bulk image-sizing pass. Bumps converter 1.20.0 to 1.21.0.

Batch 2 defect fix: type ramp censused instead of sampled (task #30). Audit Step 6 type-ramp bullet rewritten from sampling ('each of their text styles mapped') to a full census: enumerate every distinct (family, size, weight, line-height) tuple in the file, cluster within a point or two, treat each cluster as one ramp row. On a file with text styles the census is the styles page plus local overrides; on a file without text styles it is a walk over every text node in every design surveyed in Step 2. Report Brand foundations section note updated to say the ramp rows come from the census, not from sampled content modules. Rationale: Batch 2 ran the old skill and missed the nav-link style (15px bold) and quote style (24/38) because they never appeared in body-copy modules; the ratio test still passed because the missing sizes fell inside the existing range, so the arithmetic gate caught a distorted ramp but not an incomplete one. Census still runs on REFERENCE ONLY sources (the typefaces and weights the source uses are the palette the standard ramp gets mapped onto; sizes are discarded on that tier). Bumps audit 1.14.0 to 1.15.0.

Batch 2 headline defect fix: spacing system census + consistency enforcement (task #27). Audit Step 6 replaces the sampled 'spacing scale from padding/spacer components' bullet with a full census read from every module in Step 5, clustered by role (section side padding, vertical rhythm, gutter, card or inset padding, mobile equivalents). Step 7 report gets a new required 'Spacing system' section between Scale factor and Module inventory, same shape as Scale factor (census, proposed system, outliers, designer decision). Any mobile value > 160px flagged. Converter Phase 2 now states every module builds on the audit's Spacing system, not per-module source values; Phase 3 step 5 verification walks the built module and asserts every side padding, vertical padding and gutter resolves to a system value (or a named exception), and flags mobile paddings > 160px. Named exceptions (full-bleed image bands, wide-quote outsets) allowed only where the audit listed them. Bumps audit 1.13.0 to 1.14.0 and converter 1.19.3 to 1.20.0. Batch 2 ran the old skills and passed every batch report while shipping 30 distinct side insets across 28 modules, one broken on mobile (220/221 on a 320 viewport): the per-module measurement was exactly how it happened.

Six more ESP source adapters added (Brevo, Kit, ActiveCampaign, Iterable, Omnisend, HubSpot), one per ESP verified via web search (Aug 2026) to have an official MCP. Each adapter written against public MCP docs and directs the agent to introspect the connected MCP's tools at session start since no loaded tool signatures were available to verify names. Per-ESP quirks named (Brevo full-account API key, Kit's three content pools, ActiveCampaign DND vs HTML, Iterable beta/self-hosted, Omnisend product-block placeholders, HubSpot smart content and CTA library). Step 0 now has 13 source options. Bumps audit 1.12.0 to 1.13.0.

ESP migration v1.5: Google Drive + SharePoint cloud-source adapters added. Both use the same 'walk a location via MCP, pull HTML/EML/PNG, feed downstream' pattern as Local Folder. Drive adapter uses the reference Google Drive MCP with the drive.readonly scope caveat named. SharePoint adapter uses a Microsoft Graph MCP with the enterprise-IT-blocking-OAuth friction named. Step 0 gets choices (f) Google Drive and (g) SharePoint. Bumps audit 1.11.3 to 1.12.0.

ESP migration v1 commit 4: Customer.io Source adapter added (final adapter of v1 series). Uses cio_read_api + cio_schema + cio_prime. Directs cio_prime call every session, cio_auth_status for env confirmation. Names 'Automations in UI == campaigns in API' product-naming trap. v1 pulls Templates and Newsletters (customer picks one or both). Schema-first: use cio_schema to get current list/get shapes since CIO evolves the API frequently. Explicit v1 non-goals for customer transparency: does NOT pull Automations messages, Transactional, Design Studio emails, Layouts, or Snippets. Warns against reading CIO's own agent skills (design-studio, fly-api) mid-audit. Step 0 Customer.io load-reference stub updated to point to the real section.

ESP migration v1 commit 3: Marketo Source adapter added, prioritized ahead of Customer.io for an enterprise onboarding on Marketo scheduled 2026-08-05. No Marketo MCP exists, so adapter uses direct REST with OAuth 2.0 client-credentials: one-time credential collection (Munchkin ID, client ID, client secret, optional workspace), auth with token caching, list emailTemplates paginated by offset with status=approved sort locally by updatedAt, get emailTemplate/{id}/content, headless-Chrome render to PNG, design-converter worker. Rate limits (100/20s, 10K/day) explicit; adapter directs serial fetch. Marketo-specific report additions: template ID, direct edit URL, folder path, workspace. Named v1 caveat: pulls Templates only, not Emails or Content Blocks. Step 0 updated to add Marketo as (d), Customer.io renumbered to (e).

ESP migration v1 commit 2: Klaviyo Source adapter added. Uses official Klaviyo MCP for discover (get_account_details + list_email_templates with -updated sort, pagination), fetch (get_email_template returning HTML, then headless-Chrome render to PNG, then design-converter worker). Deliberately avoids render_email_template due to its 3/s burst rate limit. Report carries Klaviyo template ID, direct edit URL, and editor_type per row. v1 pulls templates only, not campaigns/flows.

ESP migration v1 commit 1: audit skill no longer assumes Figma. New Step 0 source selector, plus a Local Folder Source adapter with Discover, Fetch, and audit-step adaptations. Report shape for non-Figma sources is deliberately slimmer. Klaviyo and Customer.io adapters land in commits 2 and 3 of the v1 series.

Batch 1 fixes across converter and audit skills. Converter: mandatory mobile-decision checkpoint that runs on every module (not only when a mobile twin exists), concrete visual tells for the mj-group rule, step 5 verification that fails on missing stacking decisions, mobile-width screenshot in the visual check, and wrapper instance sizing (FIXED not FILL, on the component and every instance). Audit: lockup rows added to the recognized build-constraints vocabulary.

renderSpecIsCanonical: The render rules (structure.md and references/render-spec.md here) are the single source of truth. The Codex plugin carries mirrored copies. When a render rule changes, change it here first, then regenerate the Codex references rather than hand-editing them, so the two cannot disagree.
